explanations: C-1. Compared with no Coralia Emergency Pricing Act, price paid for buyers.inland rises from the medium run onward (tier B, invisible). Why: PC-1: a ceiling held below the price the market would reach binds sellers; where new contracts are priced freely, fewer vacancies raise their initial price instead of leaving a shortage; PC-3: those who hold a covered unit pay the controlled price, while those shut out look elsewhere; RS-4: shut-out buyers turn to uncovered units, which are close substitutes. answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-006 (illustrative figures), A-1 (binding).

question.text: At the dates the rule takes effect and over the following years, is the maximum price below the price the market would otherwise reach for the covered units?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-3 (enforcement): the Attorney General enforces actively in the declared area, including against outside sellers.

question.text: Will most of the bound sellers comply with the ceiling in practice (given whatever body enforces it, its powers, and how violations come to light)?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-6 (expectations, 0.55): local sellers can store durable goods and are not required to sell, so they can keep stock off the market until the cap lapses. WE-006 A-4 (0.9, goods can be sold elsewhere at normal prices) is about outside sellers, who are not the bound role named in this record (sellers.local), so A-6 is the row used.

question.text: Can the bound sellers move the covered resources to uses the ceiling does not reach (sale to owner-occupiers, conversion, redevelopment, keeping units off the market)?

answer.rationale: No row. Estimate from the record: the goods sold to buyers.served (generators, water, plywood) carry no right tied to holding; WE-006 A-8 (0.85) concerns rooms and is used for k3.

question.text: Is the right to buy at the controlled price tied to keeping the good (a sitting tenancy), so that the holder cannot sell or assign it?

answer.rationale: No row. Estimate from the record: a hotel is not likely to pay guests to leave a capped room, so buyouts move fewer guests than the cap keeps in place.

question.text: Will payments from landlords to sitting tenants for giving up the tenancy (buyouts) move fewer tenants than the cap keeps in place?

answer.rationale: No row. Estimate from the record: a 30-day emergency; protected buyers do not leave the area because of the cap.

question.text: Without the rule, would some of the protected buyers have moved out of the area (priced out by market rents, or for opportunities elsewhere)?

answer.rationale: No row; estimate from the record (not applicable to a 30-day emergency).

question.text: For tenants who keep a covered unit, does the lock-in outweigh moves out of the area by tenants who still move and face higher free rents in the city?

answer.rationale: No row; estimate from the record (not applicable).

question.text: Taking all protected tenants together, will the fall in moves out of the area among those who keep their units be larger than the rise among those displaced by conversion or withdrawal?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-13 (substitutability): some unserved buyers have substitutes (ice, relatives' homes).

question.text: Are uncovered units in the same market close substitutes for covered units, for buyers who cannot obtain a covered one?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-19: when local stores sell out, some residents drive between stores and look for informal sellers; the premise of C-16.

question.text: Is there no public list or allocation rule that assigns the covered good to buyers, so that buyers have to find sellers by their own search?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-18: stores in the declared counties ration scarce goods by per-customer limits and by serving regular or early customers; the premise of C-5.

question.text: Are sellers free to choose among applicants for the covered good by criteria of their own (income, credit, references, connections)?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-7: hotels may change services and stay conditions (the Act caps the charge only).

question.text: Can the bound sellers cut quality or maintenance below what they now supply without breaking a rule that is enforced (a code, a contract term)?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-10: some informal sales above the cap go undetected.

question.text: Will some exchanges of the covered good take place above the ceiling, disguised or illegal (key money, tie-in sales, sublets at market rent), without being caught?

answer.rationale: No row. WE-006 section 6: RS-11 was checked; the linked choice (taking jobs elsewhere) is not at stake in a 30-day emergency. Estimate from the record.

question.text: Would some valued opportunities for the protected buyers (a job, a better home) require them to give up the covered unit?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-20: bound sellers can organize to lobby at a cost lower than their stake (hotel and retail associations exist).

question.text: Can the groups with a concentrated stake in the rule (those it helps, those it burdens) organize and spend to keep or change it at a cost below their stakes?

answer.rationale: No row. WE-006 section 8: no durable capital is involved apart from the stocks themselves; TS-1 and TS-3 do not apply. Estimate from the record.

question.text: Are the assets the bound sellers use to supply the covered good durable, so that the supply of them expands only slowly?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-14 (expectations, 0.75): sellers expect the cap to bind in future storms (the law is standing).

question.text: Do buyers of the covered assets expect the rule to stay in force for many years?

answer.rationale: WE-006 A-12 (mobility): inland stores can be reached within days of landfall.

question.text: Can buyers who cannot obtain a covered unit buy in a neighbouring market outside the rule's reach at a cost (travel, time) they are willing to bear?

answer.rationale: No row; not applicable. Estimate from the record.

components.cap_unit: multiple of the seller's average price in the 30 days before the declaration, plus documented cost increases
source_sentences: The price of generators and fuel cans, bottled water, plywood, tarps and other building materials, and hotel, motel and short-term rental rooms sold or rented in the declared counties may not exceed 110% of the seller's own average price in the 30 days before the declaration.
Enforcement is funded from the Attorney General's budget.

Enforcement is funded from the Attorney General's budget.
